title.narrative: Economic Mobility and Protection of Women, Youth and Ecosystems for Resilient Fisheries - EMPoWER

description.narrative:
Artisanal fishing communities are economically resilient, socially protected, and environmentally sustainable through strengthened savings and cooperative management, adoption of digital IUU reporting systems, diversification of value-added enterprises, and the reduction of high-risk migration, child labour and trafficking, and gender-based violence.
Outcome 1: Aquaculture is transformed into a viable economic sector by increasing domestic fish production to reduce reliance on imports and strengthen national food security Outcome 2: Sustainable livelihoods and inclusive economic growth of artisanal fishers is enhanced through investments in job creation, entrepreneurship and cooperative development Outcome 3: Product quality of the artisanal fisheries sector is enhanced with emphasis on clean cooking and improved nutrition Outcome 4: Socio-economic conditions among women and youth across the aquatic food value chain are improved through the promotion of supplementary and alternative livelihoods in artisanal fishing communities Outcome 5: Efficiency and sustainability in Ghana's small-scale fisheries and aquaculture sectors are improved through digitalisation and innovation advancements
The Hen Mpoano projec integrates gender-responsive strategigies such as inclusive livelihoods, leadership training for women, and partnerships with women-focused organizations to ensure equitable participation and empowerment in climate adaptation efforts. The project will contribute to climate adaptation by enhancing coastal ecosystem resilience, promoting gender-inclusive livelihoods, and strengthening community governance to reduce vulnerability to climate-related risks.
Primary target groups are: Women and youth, specifically those engaged in the post-harvest value chain of small-scale fisheries and aquaculture. Artisanal fishing communities
Other target groups are: Aquaculture Farmers and Processors Community Co-Management Groups
